Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 83, verse 7–17:

﴿Nay, indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin.﴾ Regarding (kallā) there are two views:

First: it means "truly" (ḥaqqan).

Second: that kallā is for rebuke and admonition (al-zajr wa al-tanbīh).

As for (sijjīn), there are eight opinions:

The first: it means in a low place (safāl), said by al-Ḥasan.

The second: it means in loss (khasār), said by ʿIkrimah.

The third: beneath the seventh earth, narrated by al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib as a marfūʿ report.

Ibn Aslam said: Sijjīn is the lowest earth, and Sijjīl is the lowest heaven of this world.

Mujāhid said: Sijjīn is a rock in the seventh earth, and the record of the wicked is placed beneath it.

The fourth: it is a pit in Hell. Abū Hurayrah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Al-Falaq is a pit in Hell that is covered, and Sijjīn is a pit in Hell that is open."

The fifth: that it is beneath the cheek of Iblis, said by Kaʿb al-Aḥbār.

The sixth: that it is a black stone beneath the earth in which the spirits of the disbelievers are recorded, related by Yaḥyā ibn Sallām.

The seventh: that it means "the severe," said by Abū ʿUbaydah, who recited:

"A blow over which the brave made a pact, severe (sijjīnan)."

The eighth: that it means the prison (al-sijn). It is on the pattern fiʿīl from sajantuhu, and it carries intensification. This was said by al-Akhfash ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā. There is nothing preventing this from being the original meaning, with the differing interpretations concerning its place.

It may also admit a ninth: because it occupies a place of rebuke and humiliation through turning away from it and distancing from it. ﴿A written record.﴾ Regarding this there are three interpretations:

The first: it is inscribed (maktūb), said by Abū Mālik.

The second: that it is sealed (makhtūm), which is the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk.

The third: a line has been marked for them, so that no one is added to them and no one is subtracted from them, said by Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb and Qatādah.

It may also admit a fourth view: that al-marqūm means al-maʿlūm (the known).

﴿Nay, rather, what they have been earning has rusted over their hearts.﴾ Regarding this there are four interpretations:

The first: that (rān) means it sealed (ṭabaʿa) over their hearts, said by al-Kalbī.

The second: it overpowered their hearts, said by Ibn Zayd, and from it is the poet's saying:

"How many a sin has rusted over the heart of a wicked person, yet he repented of the sin that had rusted over him and it was cleared away."

The third: the successive arrival of sin upon sin until the heart becomes blind, said by al-Ḥasan.

The fourth: that it is like rust that covers the heart like a thin cloud, and this is the view of al-Zajjāj.

**Commentary of al-Mawardi (*al-Nukat wa al-Uyun*) on Surah 83, verses 18–28:**

﴿Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyun.﴾ On this there are five opinions. The first: ʿIlliyyun is Paradise. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: it is the seventh heaven. This was said by Ibn Zayd. Qatada said: the spirits of the believers are in it.

The third: it is the right pillar of the Throne. This was said by Kaʿb.

The fourth: it means being on high and ascending to God, Exalted is He. This was said by al-Hasan.

The fifth: it is the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha). This was said by al-Dahhak.

It may also be a sixth: that He describes it thus because it occupies an elevated place of acceptance.

﴿You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss.﴾ On this there are three opinions. The first: it is freshness and radiance. This was said by Ibn Shajara.

The second: it is whiteness. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The third: it is a spring in Paradise in which they perform ablutions and bathe, and the radiance of bliss flows over them. This was said by ʿAli.(p-230)

It may also be a fourth: that it is the continuation of joy through the lasting of blessing.

﴿They will be given to drink of a sealed wine.﴾ Concerning *al-Raheeq* (the pure drink) there are three opinions. The first: it is a spring in Paradise mixed with musk. This was said by al-Hasan.

The second: it is a white drink with which they seal their drinking. This was said by Ibn Abi al-Darda'.

The third: it is wine, according to the majority. From this is the verse of Hassan:

> They are given to drink from the wine of al-Baris, over them flows the Barada, clapping with the smooth *raheeq*.

However, they differed over which wine it is, in four opinions. The first: it is the purest. This was related by Ibn ʿIsa.

The second: it is the most refined and finest wine. This was said by al-Khalil.

The third: it is the wine free of adulteration. This was related by al-Akhfash.

The fourth: it is the aged wine.

Concerning *makhtum* (sealed) there are three opinions. The first: it is mixed. This was said by Ibn Masʿud.

The second: it is sealed in its vessel with a seal, and this is the apparent meaning.

The third: what Ubayy ibn Kaʿb narrated, who said: "It was said, 'O Messenger of God, what is the sealed *raheeq*?' He said: '(The pools/streams of wine).'"

﴿Its seal is musk.﴾ On this there are four interpretations. The first: its mixture is musk. This was said by Mujahid.

The second: its final outcome is musk, and *khitamuhu* means its last part, as the poet said:

> Pure wine that shimmers in the tavern, its inner part, with dark pepper and pomegranate, sealed.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 83, verses 29–36:

﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting (fakihin).﴾ ʿĀṣim, in the transmission of Ḥafs, read fākihīn without an alif, and others read it with an alif. Both readings admit four interpretations. The first: joyful (farihin), as said by al-Suddi.

The second: pleased with themselves (muʿjabin), as said by Ibn ʿAbbas, and from it is the verse of the poet:

"And I have taken my fill (fakihtu) of this world, so fight on the Day of Thursday without any visible weapon."

The third: heedless (lahin).

The fourth: luxuriant, at ease (naʿimin). ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā related these two interpretations.

ʿAwf related from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Your Lord, mighty and majestic, says: 'By My might, I will not combine for My servant two fears, nor will I combine for him two securities. If he fears Me in the world, I will grant him security on the Day of Resurrection; and if he feels secure from Me in the world, I will make him fearful on the Day of Resurrection.'"

﴿Have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do?﴾ This is the question of the believers in Paradise about the disbelievers when they parted from them. In it there are two interpretations:

One of them: its meaning is, "Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to know in disbelief?" as said by Qatadah.

The second: "Have the disbelievers been requited for what they used to do?" as said by Mujahid.

Thus (thuwwiba) would be derived from the granting of reward (ithaʾ al-thawab).

It may also admit a third interpretation: that its meaning is, "Have the disbelievers returned in the Hereafter from their denial in the world," in the sense of reproach, and it would be derived from al-mathab, which is return, not from al-thawab, which is recompense, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when We made the House a place of return (mathabatan) for the people﴾, meaning a place of return (marji'an).

It may admit a fourth interpretation: "Have they returned from the punishment of the disbelievers for what they used to do?" because they knew that they had been punished, and it was possible that they might suppose, in the generosity of Allah, that they had been shown mercy.
